title: Water Intake Calculator
description: Estimate how much water you should drink daily based on your body weight, exercise, and climate.

formula.summary: A common baseline is about 33 ml of water per kilogram of body weight, with additions for exercise and hot climates that increase fluid loss through sweat.
formula.expression: Water (L) = weight(kg) × 0.033 + exercise adjustment + climate adjustment

faqs.question: Does this include water from food and other drinks?
faqs.answer: No - this estimates total fluid needs, which you can get from water, other beverages, and water-rich foods. Roughly 20% of daily water intake typically comes from food.

faqs.question: Is more water always better?
faqs.answer: No - drinking far beyond your needs can dilute electrolytes and, in extreme cases, cause hyponatremia. This calculator gives a reasonable target, not a floor to keep exceeding.

seoContent.heading: Why water needs vary by person
seoContent.body: Body size, activity level, and climate all change how much fluid you lose and need to replace each day. A larger person generally needs more water than a smaller one, and both exercise and hot weather increase fluid loss through sweat, which is why this calculator adjusts for both.

seoContent.heading: Signs you may not be drinking enough
seoContent.body: Thirst, dark urine, fatigue, and headaches can all signal mild dehydration. This calculator gives a solid starting target, but paying attention to your body's signals and adjusting intake on hotter or more active days is just as important as hitting an exact number.
